channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Unattributed hackers altered pump cycles and disabled alarms at two small Colorado water systems
item.description: Colorado Gov. Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August. The attackers changed equipment settings, disabled remote access and alarms, and altered pumping cycles. Officials say the disruption was brief and caused no known impact on water treatment, water quality or public safety. The governor’s office says it cannot confirm which foreign actors were involved; federal officials are separately tracking an Iranian-backed effort against US water systems, but no link to Colorado has been confirmed. No new development — further victims, the access method or attribution — has been reported since 18 September. It remains the only confirmed OT-disruptive water incident in this edition’s window. - Colorado Governor’s office statement, 18 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by Axios Denver; SecurityWeek and Industrial Cyber follow-ups - Incident: late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] 996 Zyxel GS1900 network switches compromised in 48 countries through a flaw now in CISA KEV
item.category: Incident — Exploited network switch, CISA KEV
item.description: GreyNoise reported on 21 September that 996 Zyxel GS1900-series switches in 48 countries had been compromised through CVE-2026-7273 since about mid-August. The flaw is a stack-based buffer overflow in the switches’ web (CGI) interface that can let an unauthenticated attacker with network access run operating-system commands; firmware 2.90(XXXX.1)C0 and earlier is affected, and Zyxel released a fix in June. GreyNoise describes the actor as Chinese-speaking and links it to the actor, or a related one, behind earlier WordPress and Gitea exploitation. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 21 September with a 24 September federal deadline, now passed. In our assessment, low-cost managed switches like the GS1900 line are common at small utilities’ remote and treatment sites, where they network PLCs, HMIs and cellular modems, so this is a device class worth inventorying. - GreyNoise research, 21 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by Help Net Security; CISA KEV catalog, 21 Sep 2026 - Exploitation from mid-Aug 2026; KEV listing 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Background: July’s campaign against internet-exposed water-sector PLCs across a dozen states
item.category: Background — Context for the Colorado incident, not a new story
item.description: Background, not a new incident: the FBI and EPA warned on 30 July that malicious actors were remotely accessing internet-exposed Rockwell Automation MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers, changing IP addresses and passwords and, in some cases, altering ladder logic. Utilities in at least a dozen states were affected, with Minnesota alone counting more than 30 community water systems hit in a late-July wave; some experienced loss of monitoring, brief flooding or pressure loss before switching to manual operation. A group calling itself “APT Iran” claimed collaboration with CyberAv3ngers, an IRGC-linked unit, though officials stopped short of formal attribution. No boil-water advisories resulted. It is carried here only as context for the Colorado incident; no link between the two has been confirmed. - FBI/EPA alert, 30 Jul 2026 (primary); Cybersecurity Dive and Industrial Cyber reporting - Campaign: 26–27 Jul 2026; alert published 30 Jul 2026

item.title: [Medium] Infostealer logs hold OT or remote-access credentials tied to 258 US water utilities and vendors
item.category: Research — Infostealer credential exposure, not an intrusion
item.description: SpyCloud published an analysis on 20 September of stolen-identity data linked to 10,000 US water and wastewater utilities and their technology vendors. It found active infostealer exposure at 1,787 of those organizations, and credentials for OT or remote-access systems at 258. Tools named include TeamViewer, LogMeIn and GoToMyPC, plus SonicWall and Fortinet management portals. In one case, a single infected device at a major advanced-metering technology provider held saved logins for about 167 utility metering portals. SpyCloud stresses that it measures identity exposure, not confirmed intrusion, and ties the findings to no threat actor or campaign; exposure was concentrated in larger operators and vendors, with small utilities underrepresented. The practical risk for a small system is a vendor’s or employee’s infected computer leaking the same remote-access login the utility depends on (editorial assessment). - SpyCloud research, 20 Sep 2026 (primary); highlighted by SecurityWeek - Published 20 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI urge tighter control of ICS integrators’ remote access after a 2025 integrator breach
item.description: A joint CISA/FBI fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators” (dated 23 September, publicised 24 September), describes how malicious foreign cyber actors compromised a US industrial automation company in March–April 2025 and staged nine archives holding about 800 files of customer SCADA information, device details and schematics for exfiltration. It recommends least-privilege access for integrators, remote access that is monitored, logged and granted on demand where possible, security requirements written into contracts, an inventory of everything an integrator supplies, and practised manual operations with offline backups. The downstream customers it names are power utilities and transportation entities, not water, but small utilities that rely on one integrator for all PLC and SCADA work face the same exposure (editorial assessment). - CISA/FBI fact sheet dated 23 Sep 2026 (primary), publicised 24 Sep 2026 - Cites a Mar–Apr 2025 intrusion at an automation integrator

item.title: [High] Only 13% of network segments with OT devices are OT-only, Forescout study finds
item.description: Forescout’s Vedere Labs analysed 47,700 network segments containing more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations, Industrial Cyber reported on 24 September. Only 13% of the segments that contained OT devices were OT-only; the remainder held other device types, and almost half mixed OT with both IT and IoT devices. Utilities averaged nine devices per segment, against 29 in manufacturing and 72 in oil and gas. At small or unstaffed water sites, where one switch often carries SCADA alongside cameras, building systems and office equipment, a single compromised laptop or exposed switch can put pump and dosing controls within reach (editorial assessment). - Forescout Vedere Labs research (22 Sep 2026), reported by Industrial Cyber, 24 Sep 2026 - Published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Citrix confirms two actively exploited NetScaler zero-days (CVSS 9.5 each), ships fixes, added to CISA KEV
item.category: Advisory — Confirmed exploited remote-access zero-days, now patched, CISA KEV
item.description: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both rated CVSS 9.5, are remote-code-execution flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway under active exploitation on unmitigated appliances — vendor confirmation of the two unauthenticated zero-days watchTowr had reported unconfirmed the day before. CVE-2026-88771 is an improper-input-validation flaw and CVE-2026-88772 a memory-overflow flaw. Affected builds are ADC/Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.37, 13.1 before 13.1-64.23, and the corresponding FIPS/NDcPP builds; NetScaler 13.1 already reached End of Maintenance on 15 September. Citrix published bulletin CTX697096 with fixed builds the same day it confirmed exploitation, and CISA added both CVEs to KEV on 27 September with a 30 September federal deadline. These are not CVE-2026-19490, the August Gateway flaw already in KEV. Where a utility or its integrator uses NetScaler Gateway as the remote-access front door to SCADA or an OT network, this was a direct, now-patchable path toward control systems (editorial assessment). - Citrix security bulletin CTX697096 and CISA KEV catalog, 27 Sep 2026 (primary); reported by BleepingComputer, SecurityAffairs - Reported unconfirmed 26 Sep 2026; confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA lists a third exploited MikroTik RouterOS flaw; the routers often sit at small utilities’ remote sites
item.category: Advisory — Exploited remote-site router flaws, CISA KEV
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-67279, an SSH flaw in MikroTik RouterOS rated CVSS 6.9, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September with a 28 September federal deadline. CISA says it lets an unauthenticated client open a session channel and send an exec request, and can be chained with CVE-2026-86060 for unauthenticated exploitation. CERT Polska reported in-the-wild exploitation of a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick” from about 2 September; its 22 September technical analysis names these two flaws as the chain, giving full administrative control without a password. CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 were added to KEV on 10 September. Fixed builds are RouterOS 7.24.2, 7.23.4 and 6.49.21 (CVE-2026-67278 needs 7.24.3 or 7.23.6). Shadowserver counted more than 122,500 MikroTik devices with SSH reachable from the internet in early September. In our assessment, MikroTik routers are a common low-cost remote-access and cellular edge at small water and wastewater sites. - CISA KEV catalog, 25 Sep 2026 (primary); CERT Polska advisories, 5 Sep 2026 - Exploitation from about 2 Sep 2026; KEV additions 10 Sep and 25 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Schneider Modicon M580 controllers have a critical authentication flaw (CVSS v4.0 9.2)
item.category: Advisory — Controller authentication flaw, no known exploitation
item.description: Schneider Electric published security notice SEVD-2026-251-04 on 8 September for CVE-2026-3869, an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm (CWE-303) rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 (v3.1 9.8). It affects Modicon M580 controllers with application level below 4.00 and M580 Safety controllers below 4.20. No exploitation has been reported and it is not in KEV. The M580 is used for process control in water and wastewater among other sectors, including treatment and pump-station automation (editorial assessment). The fix is a firmware update plus an application-level change, which on a running treatment process needs a maintenance window and validation, so expect it to take longer than an IT patch. - Schneider Electric security notice SEVD-2026-251-04, 8 Sep 2026 (primary) - Published 8 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] A single malformed packet can crash TDengine, a time-series database used for industrial telemetry
item.category: Advisory — Industrial telemetry database denial-of-service, no known exploitation
item.description: Industrial Cyber reported on 25 September that Ridge Security found CVE-2026-42542, a pre-authentication denial-of-service flaw in the TDengine time-series database rated CVSS 7.5 (version not stated). An integer underflow in how the server handles RPC message lengths on TCP port 6030 lets one crafted packet crash the taosd service before any login, and repeating it can hold the database in a permanent crash loop. Versions 3.4.0.0 to 3.4.1.5 are affected; 3.4.1.6 fixes it. Ridge says it has seen no in-the-wild exploitation and knows of no public exploit code. Where a utility’s SCADA historian or monitoring pipeline uses TDengine, an attack would blind trending and alarming rather than change control (editorial assessment). - Ridge Security research (23 Sep 2026), reported by Industrial Cyber, 25 Sep 2026 - Published 23 Sep 2026
